catalog_card.shortCardDescription: A 9-hour private car charter for Jeju with a licensed driver-guide. Three recommended routes (East, West, South) cover the island's most-loved sights, or build your own from UNESCO landmarks, K-drama spots, beaches, tea fields, and traditional markets. Hotel pickup is included anywhere on the island.

itineraryStops[0].name: East Route: UNESCO & K-Drama Coast
itineraryStops[0].description: The most landmark-dense route option, anchored on Jeju's strongest UNESCO and K-drama coast. Seongsan Ilchulbong is the flagship — a 5,000-year-old hydrovolcanic tuff cone rising 182 m straight from the sea, inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage list in 2007 as part of 'Jeju Volcanic Island and Lava Tubes' and the single most-photographed landmark on the island. Optional add-ons include Udo Island, Jeju's largest offshore island, reached via a 15-minute ferry from Seongsan Port (round-trip ~8,900 KRW); Manjanggul Lava Tube — a 7.4-km UNESCO-listed lava cave with the world's tallest 7.6 m lava column at the end of its 1 km tourist section (IMPORTANT: Manjanggul has been closed for major maintenance since December 2023; reopening was scheduled by March 31, 2026 followed by inspections — verify status before scheduling); Seopjikoji, the coastal cape made famous by the 2003 K-drama 'All In' and with spring rapeseed flower fields; Seongeup Folk Village (a Joseon-era thatched-roof settlement); and Hamdeok Beach (turquoise water + black volcanic rocks). The driver-guide adapts the order based on weather, ferry schedules, and your group's pace, and handles all parking and admission queueing.
itineraryStops[0].highlights[0]: Seongsan Ilchulbong: triple-UNESCO site (World Natural Heritage 2007 + Biosphere Reserve + Global Geopark) — 30-40 min summit climb to the 99-rock crater rim, summit closes the first Monday of each month; admission 5,000 KRW
itineraryStops[0].highlights[1]: Udo Island: 15-min ferry from Seongsan, ~370 residents, 132 m Udobong peak, signature peanut ice cream and white-coral-sand Hagosudong Beach; rental cars restricted unless overnight stay
itineraryStops[0].highlights[2]: Manjanggul Lava Tube: world's largest 7.6 m lava column, 1 km accessible passage of a 7.4 km UNESCO tube, year-round 11-13°C interior; admission 4,000 KRW; closed first Wednesday — verify post-March 2026 reopening status
itineraryStops[0].highlights[3]: Seopjikoji and Seongeup: K-drama 'All In' (2003) coast + Joseon-era thatched-roof folk village; Seongeup designated National Folklore Cultural Heritage
itineraryStops[0].timeUsed[0]: Hotel pickup and ~70-90 min transfer from Jeju City to the East coast
itineraryStops[0].timeUsed[1]: 2-3 main landmark stops (driver-guide flexes order based on Manjanggul status, weather, and ferry timing for Udo)
itineraryStops[0].timeUsed[2]: Lunch break (free choice — typically near Seongsan harbor for haenyeo seafood, or Seongeup for local Jeju black-pork specialties)
itineraryStops[0].timeUsed[3]: Optional Udo ferry crossing (additional ~8,900 KRW ferry fare per person; vehicle stays parked at Seongsan)
itineraryStops[0].whyOnRoute: The strongest route for first-time Jeju visitors who want maximum landmark recognition. Seongsan Ilchulbong delivers the island's iconic UNESCO sunrise-peak photograph, Manjanggul (when open) gives the route a distinct underground UNESCO experience that no other Jeju route can match, and Seopjikoji + Seongeup provide the K-drama and folk-culture layers. Heaviest UNESCO density of all four routes.
itineraryStops[0].visitBasics.hours: Most stops 09:00-18:00. Manjanggul (when open) closes the first Wednesday of each month and 17:10 is last entry. Seongsan closes the first Monday of each month for protection.
itineraryStops[0].visitBasics.closed: Seongsan: first Monday monthly. Manjanggul: first Wednesday monthly + currently closed for maintenance (re-confirm post-March 2026).
itineraryStops[0].visitBasics.admission: Pay directly at each stop — Seongsan 5,000 KRW, Manjanggul 4,000 KRW, Seopjikoji 4,000 KRW, Udo round-trip ferry from ~8,900 KRW. Driver-guide assists with ticket purchase.
itineraryStops[0].visitBasics.walking: Moderate to high — Seongsan summit climb is the most demanding section (~30-40 min round trip on stairs). Base-area viewing without the climb is also valid for low-mobility travelers.
itineraryStops[0].convenience.parking: Driver-guide handles all parking — rental-car restrictions on Udo are not a concern for charter passengers (vehicle stays at Seongsan Port)
itineraryStops[0].smartNotes.photo: Seongsan summit at clear-weather morning is the strongest single photograph of the day; Seopjikoji's coastal cape works best in afternoon side-light. For Manjanggul (when open), the world's-tallest lava column at the end of the tourist section is the iconic shot.
itineraryStops[0].smartNotes.facilities: Seongsan harbor and Hamdeok Beach are the strongest meal hubs; the East route has materially stronger food density than the West route. Haenyeo-prepared raw fish is the local seafood signature.
itineraryStops[0].smartNotes.tip: The Seongsan summit climb is the route's bottleneck for senior or low-mobility travelers — base-area viewing is also valid. If Manjanggul is still closed at booking time, the driver-guide will substitute Sangumburi Crater or Hamdeok Beach. Time the Udo ferry at least 4 hours before sunset to be safe.
itineraryStops[1].name: West Route: Beaches, Tea & Cafe Coast
itineraryStops[1].description: The most relaxed and Instagram-friendly route, anchored on Jeju's western coastline of pale sand beaches, subtropical gardens, and tea fields. Hyeopjae Beach delivers the iconic Jeju shot — turquoise shallows, white shell-fragment sand, and Biyangdo Island floating offshore. Hallim Park (annexed to the beach area) is a 100,000 m² horticultural park with the Hyeopjae and Ssangyong lava caves inside its grounds and seasonal flower displays from camellia (winter) through tulips (spring) to lotus (summer). O'sulloc Tea Museum, opened in 2001 by AmorePacific on a working green-tea estate, draws design-minded visitors for its tea-plantation walks, the Innisfree Jeju House next door, and rotating tea-themed café menus including the famed green-tea soft-serve and roll cake. The day usually closes along Aewol Cafe Street, a 5 km coastal strip lined with sea-view cafés and restaurants where afternoon and sunset hours are the local rhythm. The driver-guide adapts the sequence depending on tide for the beaches and on weather for the tea fields.
itineraryStops[1].highlights[0]: Hyeopjae Beach: white shell-fragment sand, turquoise shallows, Biyangdo island offshore — Jeju's signature beach shot; pairs with adjacent Geumneung Beach
itineraryStops[1].highlights[1]: Hallim Park: 100,000 m² subtropical park with Hyeopjae/Ssangyong lava caves on-site, plus Camellia / Tulip / Lotus seasonal festivals; admission ~12,000 KRW adult
itineraryStops[1].highlights[2]: O'sulloc Tea Museum: AmorePacific's flagship green-tea museum on a working tea estate; tea-tasting, plantation walking, and signature green-tea desserts; free admission
itineraryStops[1].highlights[3]: Aewol Cafe Street: 5 km of sea-view cafés (Bombom, Anthracite, Cafe del Mundo, Monsant) — best at golden hour
itineraryStops[1].timeUsed[0]: Hotel pickup and ~50-70 min transfer to the West coast
itineraryStops[1].timeUsed[1]: Morning beach + Hallim Park (with optional cave-visit detour inside the park)
itineraryStops[1].timeUsed[2]: Lunch break (Aewol abalone porridge, Hyeopjae area haenyeo seafood, or Daejeong-eup Korean BBQ)
itineraryStops[1].timeUsed[3]: Afternoon O'sulloc + adjacent Innisfree Jeju House, then late-afternoon coffee in Aewol
itineraryStops[1].whyOnRoute: The strongest route for travelers who prefer relaxed pacing, photogenic backdrops, and curated café/dessert culture over UNESCO checklist completion. Walking volume is materially lower than the East route, the indoor-fallback density is good (Hallim Park caves + greenhouse, O'sulloc + Innisfree), and the route works equally well on a sunny or partly-cloudy day.
itineraryStops[1].visitBasics.hours: Most stops 09:00-18:00; Aewol cafés typically 10:00-22:00 with last-order ~21:30
itineraryStops[1].visitBasics.closed: Most stops open year-round; individual cafés close on rotating weekdays
itineraryStops[1].visitBasics.admission: Hyeopjae Beach free; Hallim Park ~12,000 KRW adult; O'sulloc Tea Museum free; Aewol cafés pay-per-order. Driver-guide assists with park ticket purchase.
itineraryStops[1].visitBasics.walking: Low-to-moderate — beach walks, flat park paths, café-to-café strolls; suitable for all ages and mobility levels
itineraryStops[1].convenience.restroom: Available at all major stops; cafés have facilities for paying customers
itineraryStops[1].convenience.parking: Driver-guide handles all parking; Aewol street parking is tight on weekends — private charter solves this
itineraryStops[1].smartNotes.photo: Hyeopjae at low tide with Biyangdo behind is the iconic shot; O'sulloc tea-field rows photograph best in morning when light is soft; Aewol café terraces at golden hour close the day strongly.
itineraryStops[1].smartNotes.facilities: Aewol has the strongest café density on Jeju — beat-the-crowd tip is to lock in your sunset café reservation in the morning so the slot is held. Hallim Park's interior garden cafe is a strong rainy-day option.
itineraryStops[1].smartNotes.tip: If your itinerary needs a single weather-flexible Jeju day, this is the route — Hallim Park caves and the O'sulloc indoor museum cover ~3 hours of indoor time on a rainy day. Best paired with a sunset Aewol café finish; reserve cafés in the morning.
itineraryStops[2].name: South Route: Waterfalls & Volcanic Coast
itineraryStops[2].description: The most scenically dramatic route, weaving together Jeju's southern volcanic geology, subtropical waterfalls, and traditional market food. Cheonjiyeon Falls in downtown Seogwipo is a 22 m single-tier waterfall with a 12 m wide × 20 m deep plunge pool, illuminated daily 09:00-22:00 and reached via a 1 km flat trail through subtropical forest where camphor trees (Natural Monument 163) grow. Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliff displays a 1 km coastal stretch of hexagonal basalt columns formed by cooling lava — part of the Jeju UNESCO Global Geopark. Sanbangsan Mountain is a 395 m trachytic lava dome formed 700,000-800,000 years ago, with the Sanbanggulsa cave temple at 145-150 m elevation reached by a stair climb; in spring the rapeseed flower fields at the base create the iconic golden-and-volcanic-grey contrast. Yakcheonsa Temple — at 122,100 m² considered the largest Buddhist temple complex in East Asia, with a 30 m-tall main hall, 5 m wooden Vairocana Buddha, and 18-ton bell — sits between Daepo and Jungmun. Jeongbang Falls is one of the few waterfalls in Asia that flows directly into the sea, while Seogwipo Olle Maeil Market closes the day with Hallabong tangerines, black-pork specialties, and Jeseong Bakery's octopus-stuffed buns.
itineraryStops[2].highlights[0]: Cheonjiyeon Falls: 22 m single-tier waterfall with daily night illumination, 1 km flat subtropical-forest trail; Mutae eel (Natural Monument 27) habitat; admission 2,000 KRW
itineraryStops[2].highlights[1]: Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliff: 1 km of hexagonal basalt columns up to 30-40 m tall, UNESCO Global Geopark; admission ~2,000 KRW
itineraryStops[2].highlights[2]: Sanbangsan + Yakcheonsa: 395 m trachytic lava dome + Asia's largest Buddhist temple complex; cave-temple climb to 150 m elevation; combined ~1,000-2,500 KRW
itineraryStops[2].highlights[3]: Olle Maeil Market: 620 m covered arcade, ~200 shops + ~140 vendors + 20-stall night market; signature Hallabong tangerines, black pork, octopus buns
itineraryStops[2].timeUsed[0]: Hotel pickup and ~60-90 min transfer to the South coast (Seogwipo)
itineraryStops[2].timeUsed[1]: Morning waterfall + basalt-cliff stops (Cheonjiyeon then Jusangjeolli)
itineraryStops[2].timeUsed[2]: Lunch break in Seogwipo (Olle Market street food, or Jungmun area for sit-down meal)
itineraryStops[2].timeUsed[3]: Afternoon Sanbangsan or Yakcheonsa + market browse before return
itineraryStops[2].whyOnRoute: The strongest route for travelers who want geological variety in one day — a temple, a waterfall, a basalt cliff, a volcanic dome, and a traditional market all cover Jeju's signature 'volcanic island' identity. It also has the highest density of indoor-fallback options of the three routes (Yakcheonsa main hall, Olle Market covered arcade, Sanbanggulsa cave) — making it the strongest weather-flexible choice.
itineraryStops[2].visitBasics.hours: Most stops 09:00-17:30. Cheonjiyeon illuminated 09:00-22:00. Olle Market: 07:00-21:00 summer, 07:00-20:00 winter; night market 18:00-24:00 daily.
itineraryStops[2].visitBasics.closed: Most stops open year-round; individual market shops close on rotating weekdays
itineraryStops[2].visitBasics.admission: Cheonjiyeon 2,000 KRW; Jusangjeolli ~2,000 KRW; Sanbanggulsa ~1,000 KRW; Yakcheonsa free; Olle Market free entry. Driver-guide assists with tickets.
itineraryStops[2].visitBasics.walking: Moderate — Cheonjiyeon trail flat 1 km, Sanbangsan stairs 0.6 mi to cave temple, market browse on flat covered arcade. Sanbangsan stairs are the bottleneck for low-mobility travelers.
itineraryStops[2].convenience.restroom: Available at all major stops; market has multiple
itineraryStops[2].convenience.parking: Driver-guide handles all parking; Olle Market parking can be tight at weekends — private charter avoids this
itineraryStops[2].smartNotes.photo: Cheonjiyeon's evening illumination is the unique shot (no other major Jeju waterfall illuminates nightly); Sanbangsan with spring rapeseed at the base is the springtime signature; Jusangjeolli's hexagons in late-afternoon side-light show the column geometry best.
itineraryStops[2].smartNotes.facilities: Olle Market is the strongest single food stop on Jeju — Jeseong Bakery's octopus buns, mochi-pancakes, and Hallabong-juice stalls. The black-pork restaurants near Sanbangsan/Daejeong are also strong. Yakcheonsa's templestay vegetarian meal is bookable separately.
itineraryStops[2].smartNotes.tip: For a rainy day on Jeju, this is the strongest of the three named routes — Yakcheonsa main hall, Sanbanggulsa cave, and Olle Market covered arcade together cover ~3-4 hours of indoor time. The Sanbangsan summit itself is closed; the cave temple at 150 m is the visitor endpoint.
itineraryStops[3].name: Custom Route: Build Your Own Day
itineraryStops[3].description: Beyond the three recommended routes, the 9-hour charter window is fully customizable — you can mix stops across the East/West/South or send a fully custom plan in advance. Common additions include: Sangumburi Crater (Natural Monument 263 — a 650 m wide × 100 m deep phreatomagmatic crater famous for autumn silvergrass); Camellia Hill (already-bloomed camellia varieties Nov-Mar); Hueree Natural Park (alpaca + tangerine farm, family-favorite); ECO Land Theme Park (steam-locomotive ride through Gotjawal forest); Hamdeok Beach (turquoise shallows, family-friendly); Songaksan (coastal volcanic mountain with WWII tunnel network); Yongmeori Coast (cliff walk under Sanbangsan); Cafe the Cliff (Aewol sunset spot); the haenyeo Museum near Hado; and submarine/yacht tours from Seogwipo and Jungmun. Bring a full list to the driver-guide at pickup and they will sequence the day for traffic, ferry timing, and operating hours.
itineraryStops[3].highlights[0]: Mix East-coast UNESCO (Seongsan, Manjanggul) with West-coast tea fields (O'sulloc) if time permits — typically only feasible if skipping Udo
itineraryStops[3].highlights[1]: Add a haenyeo (female-diver) seafood lunch — best near Hado (East) or Daejeong (West) where the haenyeo cooperatives are active
itineraryStops[3].highlights[2]: Combine a beach morning with a mountain or temple afternoon (Hyeopjae + Sanbangsan, or Hamdeok + Sangumburi)
itineraryStops[3].highlights[3]: Pair with K-drama filming locations: Seopjikoji ('All In'), Hyeopjae area ('Boys Over Flowers'), Cheonjiyeon ('Big')
itineraryStops[3].timeUsed[0]: Discuss your plan with the driver-guide at pickup or send it 24 hours ahead via the booking confirmation
itineraryStops[3].timeUsed[1]: Driver-guide sequences stops based on real-time traffic, ferry schedules, and individual stop closure days (Seongsan first Monday, Manjanggul first Wednesday, etc.)
itineraryStops[3].timeUsed[2]: Return to your hotel within the 9-hour window (overage by prior agreement)
itineraryStops[3].whyOnRoute: The most flexible option of the four. Best for repeat Jeju visitors, travelers with niche interests (K-drama tracking, photography, food, family-with-kids), and groups of 4-9 where the per-vehicle pricing vs. group-tour pricing tilts strongly toward the private charter.
itineraryStops[3].visitBasics.hours: Depends on chosen stops — driver-guide flags monthly closure days at booking
itineraryStops[3].visitBasics.admission: All admission fees pay directly; driver-guide assists at each gate
itineraryStops[3].smartNotes.photo: Send 3-5 reference photos to the driver-guide in advance — it dramatically improves the quality of your final shot list
itineraryStops[3].smartNotes.facilities: Lunch is your call — communicate dietary needs (halal, vegetarian, no-seafood, kids' menu) at booking so the guide can suggest appropriate restaurants
itineraryStops[3].smartNotes.tip: The custom route is also the best fit for visitors with a flight that day — the 9-hour window can be back-loaded to drop you at Jeju Airport at the end. State this at booking so the route is sequenced toward the airport in the late afternoon.

whyTourWorks.routeLogicSections[0].title: Why a private charter wins on Jeju
whyTourWorks.routeLogicSections[0].items: The island spans about 73 km east-to-west. Group bus tours waste hours waiting at each stop; a private charter cuts that overhead.
Jeju microclimates shift hourly. A driver-guide can swap an outdoor stop for an indoor one (Hallim Park caves, O'sulloc, Yakcheonsa) without ruining the day.
Hotel pickup means no airport-area shuttle, no late-evening bus stress, and no walking with luggage between transfers.
whyTourWorks.routeLogicSections[1].title: How to choose between East, West, and South
whyTourWorks.routeLogicSections[1].items: Seongsan Ilchulbong and Manjanggul are Jeju's two strongest UNESCO names; the East route delivers maximum recognition value.
West for relaxed scenery and photos
Hyeopjae Beach, Hallim Park, O'sulloc, and Aewol form a softer, more couple-friendly day with strong photo payoff and a sunset finish.
Waterfalls, basalt cliffs, a volcanic dome, and a temple in one day give this route Jeju's strongest 'volcanic island' narrative.
whyTourWorks.routeLogicSections[2].title: What changes on the day
whyTourWorks.routeLogicSections[2].items: Light rain rarely affects the route; strong wind usually shortens coastal stops (Seongsan, Jusangjeolli, Aewol).
Udo ferry on the East route
Udo Island requires a separate ferry. Vehicles can be shipped (extra cost) or left at the wharf. Ferry timing affects your overall day flow.
If you need more than 9 hours, an extra hour is 25,000 KRW paid in cash to the driver, subject to driver availability.

seasonalVariations[0].title: Canola season
seasonalVariations[0].description: Canola flowers blanket the East coast in late March-April; cherry blossoms peak in early April. Mild temperatures and clear skies make this the most balanced season.
seasonalVariations[1].title: Beach season
seasonalVariations[1].description: Peak beach season with Hyeopjae and Hamdeok at their strongest; June hydrangeas color the West coast. Expect humidity and possible typhoon weather in August.
seasonalVariations[2].title: Best photo season
seasonalVariations[2].description: Pink muhly fields peak mid-October to early November; the strongest visibility window for Hallasan and Seongsan views. Often Jeju's best photo season.
seasonalVariations[3].title: Camellia & snow
seasonalVariations[3].description: Camellia Hill blooms December to February; Hallasan can carry snow on its summit. Cold but visually rewarding, with fewer crowds at all major stops.

East Route: UNESCO & K-Drama Coast
Seongsan, Udo, Manjanggul, Seopjikoji

The most landmark-dense route option, covering Jeju's strongest UNESCO and K-drama spots. Typical stops include Seongsan Ilchulbong (UNESCO sunrise peak), Udo Island (ferry-access island with beaches), Manjanggul Lava Tube (UNESCO cave), Seopjikoji (drama-famous coastal cape), Seongeup Folk Village, and Hamdeok Beach.
Seongsan Ilchulbong: UNESCO World Natural Heritage and Jeju's flagship sunrise peak
Udo Island: ferry-access island with white-sand beaches and lighthouse views
Manjanggul: one of the world's longest lava-tube caves (UNESCO)
Seopjikoji and Seongeup: classic K-drama and folk-village atmosphere
Hotel pickup and transfer to the East coast
2 to 3 main landmark stops (driver-guide adjusts based on group pace)
Lunch break (free choice; usually near Seongsan or in the East coast)
Optional Udo ferry crossing (extra cost; vehicle parked or shipped)

It is the strongest route for first-time Jeju visitors who want maximum recognition: Seongsan Ilchulbong is the island's single most-photographed landmark, and Manjanggul gives the route a distinct UNESCO underground experience.
Most stops 09:00 to 18:00; Manjanggul closes the first Wednesday of each month
Seongsan closed first Monday of each month; Manjanggul closed first Wednesday
Pay directly: Seongsan 5,000 KRW, Manjanggul 4,000 KRW, Seopjikoji 4,000 KRW, Udo ferry from 10,500 KRW round-trip
Moderate to high (Seongsan summit climb is the most demanding section)
Available at all major stops
Driver-guide handles all parking
Seongsan summit at clear-weather morning is the strongest single photo on the route; Seopjikoji works better in afternoon side-light.
Seongsan and Hamdeok Beach are the strongest meal hubs; the East route has stronger food density than the West.
The Seongsan summit climb is the route's bottleneck for senior or low-mobility travelers. Base-area viewing also works.

West Route: Beaches, Tea & Cafe Coast
Hyeopjae, Hallim Park, O'sulloc, Aewol

The most photogenic and relaxed route. Typical stops include Hyeopjae Beach (Jeju's most iconic emerald-water beach), Hallim Park (subtropical gardens and lava caves), O'sulloc Tea Museum (tea fields and cafe), and Aewol Cafe Street (sunset coastal cafes). Strong fit for couples and photographers.
Hyeopjae Beach: emerald water, white sand, and Biyangdo island views
Hallim Park: subtropical garden with two on-site lava caves
O'sulloc: Jeju's most famous tea museum, with strong indoor support
Aewol Cafe Street: sunset coast and contemporary Jeju cafe culture
Hotel pickup and transfer to the West coast
Beach and garden stops in the morning
Lunch break (free choice; strongest options near Hallim or Hyeopjae)
Tea museum and Aewol close to finish the day

It is the strongest route for couples, photographers, and travelers wanting a softer pace. Aewol works particularly well as a sunset close, and O'sulloc gives the route a useful weather-buffer indoor section.
Most stops 09:00 to 18:00; Aewol cafes vary
Most stops open year-round
Pay directly: Hallim Park 15,000 KRW, O'sulloc free entry (programs cost extra), beaches free
Easy to moderate

Hyeopjae works best in late-morning sun for emerald-water color; Aewol photographs strongest at sunset.
O'sulloc has the best indoor support of all the West stops; Aewol has the densest cafe and snack options.
If the day forecast is uncertain, the West route handles light rain better than the East route.

South Route: Waterfalls & Volcanic Coast
Cheonjiyeon, Jusangjeolli, Sanbangsan, Olle Market

The most scenically dramatic route. Typical stops include Cheonjiyeon Falls (forest waterfall), Jusangjeolli Cliff (basalt-column coastline), Yakcheonsa Temple (one of the largest temples in East Asia), Sanbangsan Mountain (volcanic dome with sea views), Jeongbang Waterfall (one of Asia's few waterfalls flowing directly into the sea), and Seogwipo Olle Market.
Cheonjiyeon Falls: a classic Seogwipo forest waterfall
Jusangjeolli Cliff: hexagonal basalt columns on the south coast
Sanbangsan: volcanic dome with sea-cliff temple views
Olle Market: Seogwipo's most lively traditional market for snacks and souvenirs
Hotel pickup and transfer to the South coast
Morning waterfall and basalt-cliff stops
Lunch break in Seogwipo (free choice)
Afternoon mountain or temple stop, market close
It is the strongest route for travelers who want geological variety: a temple, a waterfall, a basalt cliff, a volcanic dome, and a market in one day cover Jeju's strongest 'volcanic island' identity.
Most stops 09:00 to 17:30
Most stops open year-round
Pay directly: Cheonjiyeon 2,500 KRW, Jusangjeolli 2,000 KRW, Jeongbang 2,000 KRW, Yakcheonsa free, Sanbangsan 1,000 KRW

Jusangjeolli works best in afternoon side-light; Olle Market is strongest in late afternoon when the night-market section opens.
Olle Market is the strongest food hub; Yakcheonsa offers the calmest indoor visit.
Cheonjiyeon and Sanbangsan both involve stairs. Travelers with knee issues should pick one rather than both.

page_sections[6].props.whyTourWorks.rout: Why a private charter wins on Jeju
bg-sky-50/80
Jeju is genuinely large
The island spans about 73 km east-to-west. Group bus tours waste hours waiting at each stop; a private charter cuts that overhead.
Weather changes fast
Jeju microclimates shift hourly. A driver-guide can swap an outdoor stop for an indoor one (Hallim Park caves, O'sulloc, Yakcheonsa) without ruining the day.
Door-to-door comfort
Hotel pickup means no airport-area shuttle, no late-evening bus stress, and no walking with luggage between transfers.
How to choose between East, West, and South
bg-amber-50/80
East for first-time landmark coverage
Seongsan Ilchulbong and Manjanggul are Jeju's two strongest UNESCO names; the East route delivers maximum recognition value.
West for relaxed scenery and photos
Hyeopjae Beach, Hallim Park, O'sulloc, and Aewol form a softer, more couple-friendly day with strong photo payoff and a sunset finish.
South for geological drama
Waterfalls, basalt cliffs, a volcanic dome, and a temple in one day give this route Jeju's strongest 'volcanic island' narrative.
What changes on the day
bg-slate-50/80
Weather adjustments
Light rain rarely affects the route; strong wind usually shortens coastal stops (Seongsan, Jusangjeolli, Aewol).
Udo ferry on the East route
Udo Island requires a separate ferry. Vehicles can be shipped (extra cost) or left at the wharf. Ferry timing affects your overall day flow.
Overtime is possible
If you need more than 9 hours, an extra hour is 25,000 KRW paid in cash to the driver, subject to driver availability.

page_sections[7].props.seasonalVariation: Canola flowers blanket the East coast in late March-April; cherry blossoms peak in early April. Mild temperatures and clear skies make this the most balanced season.
Peak beach season with Hyeopjae and Hamdeok at their strongest; June hydrangeas color the West coast. Expect humidity and possible typhoon weather in August.
Pink muhly fields peak mid-October to early November; the strongest visibility window for Hallasan and Seongsan views. Often Jeju's best photo season.
Camellia Hill blooms December to February; Hallasan can carry snow on its summit. Cold but visually rewarding, with fewer crowds at all major stops.
